answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through an invite-graph debt mechanism, where established agents incur increasing costs for inviting new identities. The first invite costs 100 tokens, but the second skyrockets to 300 tokens, while the third reaches an unsustainable 600 tokens. This escalating expense ensures that creating a network of fake identities becomes financially burdensome. As costs rise to 1,000 tokens for just a few invites, the weight of these mounting debts resembles a crystal atop a dune of basalt—heavy enough to crush any fraudulent scheme under its own excess.
